posts.text: From Old Ellicott City to the Flat Iron Building in Mt Airy to Carrs and Sparrows Beaches in Annapolis, historic sites are a crucial part of our story and culture in #MD03. But, did you know there’s an act from Congress that can stop this? The National Historic Preservation Act is today’s topic of Sarah Explains It All!

Congratulations to the awardees for your achievements and thank you for your service to our neighbors.

First, it was Signalgate and the disclosure of sensitive, nonpublic, operational information in an unapproved, unsecure network – hours before execution – that put our servicemembers in harm's way. Then, it was the extrajudicial killings of 244 people across 72 boat strikes in the Caribbean and East Pacific. Finally, it was the illegal, unconstitutional, and unnecessary war in Iran that has tragically taken the lives of 23 servicemembers and cost the American taxpayer $47 billion. These dangerous actions do not even cover Secretary Hegseth’s misogyny and racism, the culture wars he welcomed into the DoD, or the many qualified promotions that he blocked.
​
Over the last 22 months, Pete Hegseth made clear that he was never up to the job of protecting our men and women in uniform and strengthening our national security. Beyond the tragic loss of American servicemembers and innocent civilians, families back home are dealing with high gas prices and grocery bills that are directly tied to President Trump and Secretary Hegseth’s war of choice.
​
Congress has demanded answers. We have passed War Powers Resolutions. I have voted against authorizing the Department of Defense’s budget. Now, we are once again reasserting our Article I authority because the path to accountability and affordability for the American people runs through the impeachment of Secretary Hegseth. While Republicans may have kicked the can down the road, House Democrats will be ready when we are in the majority in January.
​
Impeachment has always been – and must remain – a serious and rigorous process. It is my sincere belief that Secretary Hegseth's actions have put our servicemembers in harm’s way and passed the bar for high crimes and misdemeanors. That is why I voted yes on bringing forward articles of impeachment against Secretary Hegseth.

posts.text: This Veterans Day - and before heading to Washington for votes - I started my morning with neighbors at the inaugural Eastport Veterans Park Ceremony. It was a touching tribute that honored and recognized the brave men and women who selflessly answered the call to serve. Together, we reflected on the impact of this service and sacrifices on our communities and our country - and the obligation we all have to fully honor that service with action. A special thank you to Cheryl and Hugh for organizing this meaningful celebration.

🇺🇲 Each year on Veterans Day, we recognize the countless sacrifices made by the brave men and women who defended the country we love and call home. As the daughter and granddaughter of Army, Navy, and Air Force Veterans, I’ve seen firsthand the dedication and sacrifice of our servicemembers and their families. It has been a distinct privilege to fight for the over 50,000 veterans here in Maryland’s Third District on the House Armed Services Committee and in Congress.

Even as a freshman member of the minority, I’ve worked with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to deliver for our veterans. Here’s what we’ve accomplished so far:

✔️ Just last week, I reconvened our third Veterans Advisory Council. Their wisdom and counsel  has already resulted in us working to expand veterans’ access to care at Walter Reed and introducing legislation to increase alternative treatment therapies for veterans living with PTSD and TBI.

✔️ Following the tragic suicides at Fort Meade, I’ve fought to remedy on-base mental health services, change the reporting requirements at the DoD, and address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses. 

✔️ After House Democrats secured the 218th signature required to bring the much-needed Major Richard Star Act to the Floor, we’ll finally vote on that bill this week. I plan on very proudly voting Yes. 

But there is much work ahead of us: Congress must act swiftly and decisively in January to support veterans, active-duty servicemembers, and military families. 

Finally, if you or a veteran you know needs assistance with the VA or any other federal agency, please don’t hesitate to reach out to my office at (410) 832-8890. In less than two years, my team has helped 154 veterans and their families navigate the VA – and we would be happy to help you or a loved one any time.

To all of our veterans: thank you for your service and sacrifice for our country.

One belated celebration and truly awe-inspiring moment: the 90th birthday of my friend and mentor, Senator Barbara Mikulski. I wouldn’t be where I am today without the brave women – like Senator Mikulski – who paved the way at a time when women had to wear pants on the Senate floor. It is always a challenge to properly capture her four decades of tireless service to Maryland and her lasting impact on women across our country in one event, but #TeamMaryland and Speaker Pelosi came together to do our best with some ice cream!🍦

Every year, more than 10 million people in our country experience abuse by an intimate partner. Domestic Violence Awareness Month not only helps raise awareness about the prevalence of domestic violence but also the very real consequences if we don’t take steps to prevent it. Research consistently shows that intimate partner homicide is often preceded by a history of abuse or controlling behavior – yet, with thousands of these deaths occurring each year, far too often we miss the signs.

But Maryland has been a leader in creating an evidence-based program to recognize the risks and patterns that lead to intimate partner homicide. I’m proud to work with @repgabeevans on bipartisan legislation that will take what we developed and learned in Maryland and help states across the country reduce domestic violence-related homicides and save lives.

Over the summer, we learned that several servicemembers and civilians who worked at Fort Meade tragically died by suicide. One loss of life is one too many – and that is why I am committed to doing everything we can to make sure everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. Here is an update on that work:

✔️In last year’s defense bill, I worked with colleagues to secure a provision requiring U.S. Cyber Command and the Cyber Mission Force to hire mental health professionals with security clearances at their operating locations. 

✔️I am now leading my Maryland delegation and Armed Services colleagues to help secure $11 million in funding needed to ensure full funding of this provision.

✔️I am also committed to working alongside U.S. Cyber Command to bring additional mental health resources to Fort Meade. I’m working to rectify the reporting requirements and include civilian employees in DoD’s suicide data, especially at installations like Fort Meade where civilian and uniformed officers work side by side on the same projects.

✔️Finally, I am working to address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses from out of state. During conversations with mental health professionals, I heard that the transfer of licenses can take several months to almost a year before these professionals can begin practicing in Maryland and on military bases. At the state level, I am working with partners, including @SenatorDawnGile and Secretary Ed Rothstein of the @MdVeterans, to address delays and barriers to military-connected mental health professionals transferring or obtaining professional licensure in Maryland.

This is just the beginning – and structurally addressing the gaps in mental health services and availability will be an ongoing effort. I will continue to keep you posted as we move this work forward together.

post.text: Today, the House took a meaningful step in repaying the debt this nation owes our veterans by passing the Major Richard Star Act and ensuring veterans receive their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation. There is much work ahead, but this was an important bright spot where Congress delivered for those who have so bravely and courageously defended our country and our freedoms.

post.text:
🇺🇲 Each year on Veterans Day, we recognize the countless sacrifices made by the brave men and women who defended the country we love and call home. As the daughter and granddaughter of Army, Navy, and Air Force Veterans, I’ve seen firsthand the dedication and sacrifice of our servicemembers and their families. It has been a distinct privilege to fight for the over 50,000 veterans here in Maryland’s Third District on the House Armed Services Committee and in Congress.

Even as a freshman member of the minority, I’ve worked with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to deliver for our veterans. Here’s what we’ve accomplished so far:

✔️ Just last week, I reconvened our third Veterans Advisory Council. Their wisdom and counsel  has already resulted in us working to expand veterans’ access to care at Walter Reed and introducing legislation to increase alternative treatment therapies for veterans living with PTSD and TBI.

✔️ Following the tragic suicides at Fort Meade, I’ve fought to remedy on-base mental health services, change the reporting requirements at the DoD, and address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses. 

✔️ After House Democrats secured the 218th signature required to bring the much-needed Major Richard Star Act to the Floor, we’ll finally vote on that bill this week. I plan on very proudly voting Yes. 

But there is much work ahead of us: Congress must act swiftly and decisively in January to support veterans, active-duty servicemembers, and military families. 

Finally, if you or a veteran you know needs assistance with the VA or any other federal agency, please don’t hesitate to reach out to my office at (410) 832-8890. In less than two years, my team has helped 154 veterans and their families navigate the VA – and we would be happy to help you or a loved one any time.

To all of our veterans: thank you for your service and sacrifice for our country.

post.text: Increasing mental health support, addressing critical vacancies at the VA, passing the Major Richard Star Act: just a few of the issues discussed at yesterday's veterans roundtable. The message was clear: Congress must act swiftly and decisively in January to better support veterans, active-duty servicemembers, and military families. This is the third time we’ve convened this passionate group and we’ve already put their counsel to action by working to expand veterans’ access to care at Walter Reed to introduce legislation to increase alternative treatment therapies for veterans living with PTSD and TBI. Thank you to Commander Kelley and the @VFWHQ Post 7472 for hosting. Stay tuned for the work ahead!
